sections.title: Welcome to {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: {{guild_name}} is a community of quilters in {{city}} who share a love of fabric, color, and craft. Whether you have been quilting for decades or are threading your first needle, you are welcome here.

sections.heading: Guild night
sections.where: Sample text — replace me: the community center in {{city}}
sections.note: Guests are welcome at their first meeting, no dues required. Doors open thirty minutes early for show and tell setup.

items.title: Bees
items.body: Small groups that meet between guild nights to sew together, swap fabric, and finish what we started. Day bees, evening bees, and a hand-work bee.

items.title: Block of the month
items.body: One block, one set of instructions, and a drawing at the meeting for the finished set. A gentle way to try a new technique every month.

items.title: Charity quilts
items.body: Comfort quilts for the children's hospital in Austin, foster families, and veterans in our county. Kits are ready to pick up at every meeting.

items.title: Workshops
items.body: Hands-on classes with visiting teachers, from foundation paper piecing to free-motion quilting, at member rates.

sections.title: Join {{guild_name}}
sections.body: Sample text — replace me: Dues are collected once a year and include monthly programs, the newsletter, the lending library, and a place in the annual show.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Quilters in {{city}} and the surrounding Hill Country, meeting since 1984 to share the craft.

sections.heading: Our story
sections.html:
Sample text — replace me: Tell your story here. When was the guild founded, and by whom? Many Central Texas guilds started as a handful of friends trading patterns at a kitchen table; others grew out of a county extension class or a church sewing circle. Say what kinds of quilting members enjoy: traditional piecing, hand appliqué, modern, art quilts, hand quilting.

{{guild_name}} welcomes every skill level. Beginners learn from members who have been quilting for fifty years, and long-time members pick up new techniques from people who started last spring.

items.title: Monthly programs
items.body: Guest speakers, trunk shows, and demonstrations at every guild night.

items.title: Workshops and retreats
items.body: Weekend retreats in the Hill Country and hands-on classes with visiting teachers.

items.title: The annual show
items.body: Members' quilts judged and displayed each spring, with a viewer's choice ribbon.

items.title: Community projects
items.body: Comfort quilts, pillowcases, and Quilts of Valor delivered across the county.

items.title: Children's hospital
items.body: Crib and lap quilts for the NICU and pediatric units in Austin.

items.body: Presented to veterans in our county at a ceremony each November.

items.body: Pillowcases and twin quilts through the county child welfare office.

items.title: Memory care
items.body: Lap quilts and fidget quilts for residents of local nursing homes.

sections.heading: How to help
sections.html:
Sample text — replace me: Pick up a kit at any meeting, sew the top at home, and bring it back. Longarm members quilt the tops; a binding bee finishes them. Donations of cotton fabric and batting are always welcome.

Charity sew days happen on the second Saturday of the month at the community center. Bring your machine, a cutting mat, and a lunch.

sections.title: Sew with us
sections.body: You do not have to be a member to sew a comfort quilt, but members get the kits first.
